title: Burst variance prober and contract attestation
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Summary:
We need a reproducible, tenant-aware load prober that measures burst variance and validates Dedicated capacity throughput SLAs for customer-facing acceptance. This ticket defines the prober design, benchmarking methodology, and the customer acceptance protocol that pairs a deterministic harness with an agreed signoff checklist. Goals: measure committed QPS under bursty arrival patterns, verify SLOs for tail latency and error rate, validate autoscaler safety bounds, and produce artifacts customers can use for acceptance testing.

Background / Motivation:
Customers buying Dedicated capacity require deterministic throughput guarantees (committed QPS and tail latency). Existing replay tools focus on steady-state QPS or generic ramp profiles; they miss real-world burst variance (microbursts + mid-length surges + cold-starts). We need tooling that: (1) synthesizes realistic burst profiles and tenant mixes, (2) drives the fleet in a way that exercises autoscaler and fallback controls, and (3) emits a standardized evidence bundle for contract attestation.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: harness code, test scenarios, metric definitions, runbook for customer acceptance runs, dashboards/plots, standard report template for signoff.
- Out of scope: changes to scheduler/kernels (separate RFC), long-term storage of all traces (we'll link to existing tracing infra), and new billing models.

Key deliverables:
- Burst Variance Prober (BVP) API & CLI that can run synthetic and replay scenarios against a Dedicated pool.
- Benchmark methodology doc: scenarios, measurement windows, warmup, cooldown, tolerances.
- Customer Acceptance Checklist and Evidence Bundle template (PRs, dashboards, CSV of runs, annotated results).

Success criteria:
- BVP runs reproducibly and produces the evidence bundle in < 45 minutes for standard scenario.
- For baseline scenario (committed QPS X): sustained throughput >= X for 60 minutes with error rate < 0.1% and p99 latency below contract threshold in >= 9/10 runs.
- Autoscaler behavior validated: scale-up triggers in < 120s for target load spike, scale-down holds at least 10 minutes to avoid flapping.

Notes on nomenclature: committed QPS refers to the contract QPS for the customer's Dedicated pool. Burst = any sub-minute increase >= 3x baseline QPS. Surge = multi-minute elevated traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: BVP produces structured evidence bundle (run metadata, raw telemetry link, summary CSV, consolidated dashboard URL)
Standard scenario: 60m sustain at committed QPS with error rate < 0.1% and p99 <= contract threshold in 9/10 independent runs
Burst scenario: 30s microburst at 4x baseline observed, system maintains tail SLOs or fails over gracefully to fallback model with no data leakage
Autoscaler: scale-up reaction time <= 120s for a preconfigured spike, scale-down cooldown >= 600s
QA run and Engineering review completed, and customer signoff recorded in the evidence bundle

approach_and_methodology:
Overview:
We will combine synthetic and replay strategies. Synthetic scenarios allow controlled variance (deterministic seeds) and tenant mixes; replay runs validate fidelity against customer traces. The harness will be parameterizable: tenant_count, baseline_qps, burst_profile (amplitude, duration, inter-burst spacing), request_size_distribution, model_variant_selector.

Measurement windows:
- Warmup: 5 minutes (ignore telemetry for final numbers)
- Measurement: 60 minutes for sustain scenarios, 15-20 minutes for short-surge acceptance runs
- Cooldown: 5 minutes

Metrics captured per run:
- Aggregate throughput (requests/s) per 1s and 1m windows
- Error count and error types (timeouts, 5xx, rate-limit)
- Latency histograms (p50, p90, p95, p99, p999) for generation steps and end-to-end
- Autoscaler events: timestamped scale actions, instance counts, reasons
- KV cache hit ratio and observed cold-start penalties

Pass/fail logic:
Compute pass flags across metric windows; annotate failures with deterministic evidence (trace IDs, stack traces, node IDs). All rules encoded in the harness so runs are machine-verifiable.
test_scenarios: Baseline sustain: baseline_qps = committed_QPS; duration 60m; validate sustained throughput and p99
Microburst flood: 30s spikes at 4x baseline every 10m across randomized tenant subset
Surge taper: 10m ramp to 2.5x baseline then 20m sustain then 10m ramp down
Cold-start storm: simultaneous cold cache traffic pattern from >50% of tenants to exercise kernel warmup and KV priming
Tenant-slice isolation: high load on one tenant while neighbors maintain baseline to validate QoS safeguards
automation_and_integration:
CI: add nightly stochastic runs to detect regressions in burst variance handling.
Orchestration: BVP will run as a container job that posts results to the evidence-bucket and emits a signed manifest to the console.
PR hooks: tests for new scheduler/autoscaler commits must run the short microburst scenario as part of the PR pipeline.
Telemetry: use existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus histograms + traces) and tag runs with run_id and ticket key.
runbook_for_customer_acceptance:
Pre-run checklist:
- Confirm dedicated pool id and committed_QPS in the agreement
- Agree on dataset: synthetic seed vs. customer replay trace
- Decide fallback policies (model variant mapping, routing failover) to exercise during run
- Schedule 2h window and ensure on-call coverage from infra and solutions engineering

During run:
- Start harness with run_id and email signoff link to customer
- Monitor dashboard (throughput, latency, instance count) and log autoscaler events in a shared channel
- If a critical failure occurs, pause run and collect diagnostic bundle (node logs, traces)

Post-run deliverables:
- Evidence bundle (manifest + CSV + dashboard + annotated logs)
- Signoff template for customer to confirm pass/fail on agreed criteria
- Optional remediation action list if any criteria failed
